- Model consistently overestimates early in the forecast horizon, especially in the first 5–10 days, then underestimates later — suggest adjusting for mean reversion toward historical median.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >85), model tends to overshoot and overforecast for 2–3 days — apply dampening factor or lagged smoothing to prevent overreaction.
- Model underestimates when true price drops below 80 — may be missing downward momentum or policy-driven volatility — add downward bias correction for low-price regimes.
- Forecast tends to lag true price by 1–3 days in downward trends — consider rolling 3-day moving average to align with actual price direction.
- Model often fails to capture short-term volatility spikes — especially in 5–10 day windows — introduce volatility-weighted adjustment or use rolling standard deviation to scale forecast error.
